19. At a macro level, the data unequivocally shows that the actual average daily outage across
   all assessed categories outpaces the utility's scheduled load shedding limits. The most
    critical deviations are observed in the High and Very High Loss categories, where actual
   outages exceed the declared 10-hour limit by substantial margins. The Authority provides
   a detiled category-wise analytical breakdown as follows:

A staggering 68.4% of the feeders (91 out of 133) in this category experienced outages
lasting between 6 and over 8 hours daily. Consequently, 71.4% of the consumers
(346,243 individuals) classified under the Medium Loss category are subjected to an
average daily outage of more than 6 hours, breaching the utility's maximum prescribed
limit of 6 hours.

The data for the High Loss category (171 feeders) demonstrates a systemic failure to
cap load shedding at the scheduled 10-hour mark. The actual average daily outage for
this category stands at 10 hours and 39 minutes. A staggering 81.9% of the feeders in
this category surpass the scheduled 10-hour limit. Specifically, 109 feeders (63.7%)
face an average of 10 hours and 38 minutes of outages, while 29 feeders (17.0%) endure
extreme outages averaging 12 hours and 39 minutes. In the most severe cases, 2 feeders
suffer outages exceeding 14 hours, averagjgi4 hours and 14 minutes.
